pr_title: Allow using arrow keys to navigate volume controls when controls are already visible

issue_context.title: Left and right arrow keys change volume when volume overlay is focused
issue_context.body:
Not sure why they do but they seem to. Also left increases volume and right decreases.

I think when the volume controls are focused (ie. hovered), they should handle up/down/left/right using `OnKeyDown`, matching the defaults for the `Alt+` variants.

review_comments: It's 100% intentional and would be pointless otherwise. The keys you mention are already handled at a *global level* in `VolumeControlReceptor`. The bindings in this PR are local, when the control is focused, to give more control (generally without alt-prefixes).

The `VolumeControlReceptor` handles the volume binding specific ones, which are prefixed with `Alt`. While these are not prefixed with `Alt` and are generally used to traverse through a visible collection of objects (e.g. traversing beatmaps in song select).

To reiterate, this is intentional. When the volume controls are focused, I want the arrow keys to work regardless of user bindings. Without the `alt-` prefix.

Are you worried about the UX with these bindings I've added? A specific example may help better.

> To reiterate, this is intentional. When the volume controls are focused, I want the arrow keys to work regardless of user bindings. Without the alt- prefix.

I see, missed to realize this part, thinking users are constrained to arrow keys when interacting with the volume overlay, but the keybinds will still work just fine.
